title: Compact telemetry joiner and hot/cold log tiering
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: In high-throughput services we observe a gap between sampled tracing data and full structured logs. Downstream staff cannot reliably join traces to complete log contexts when sampling or ingestion ordering causes the log to be archived before a trace link is available. Current Loki ingestion pipeline also struggles with high-cardinality labels and hotspot tenants, causing inconsistent retention and query cost spikes.

Goal: Build a compact 'telemetry-joiner' service that attaches stable correlation tokens and reconciles sampled spans to full logs within the hot tier, plus implement a hot/cold log tiering path that writes compact Parquet archives for cold storage (S3), while keeping recent structured logs in Loki/Elasticsearch for fast queries. This should reduce missing span->log joins, lower query egress/ingestion cost, and provide deterministic retention per tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry-joiner attaches a stable join_token to logs and sampled spans; token persisted as log label 'join_token' and trace attribute 'join_token'
End-to-end test validates >=95% successful span-to-log linkage for synthetic traffic with 10% trace sampling (within 30s window)
Hot store (Loki/ES) ingestion latency: 90th percentile <= 2s for 90% of traffic during a 1h load test at peak qps
Cold-tier archiver writes compressed Parquet files partitioned by date/tenant and verifies checksums within 15 minutes of rollup
Dynamic tenant retention policy applied: heavy tenants can be auto-tiered to cold within policy thresholds; documented in console retention view
Comprehensive unit and integration tests, plus a runbook for failure modes and rollback steps
implementation_notes: Edge parser: normalize incoming structured logs to canonical schema (timestamp, tenant_id, trace_id, span_id, log_level, message, attributes) and emit canonical 'join_token' computed as sha256(tenant_id + trace_id + truncated_ts) to limit cardinality

Telemetry-joiner service sits in the ingest path after parser; maintains an in-memory LRU cache mapping join_token -> freshest(log_id, offset) for quick joins; persists tombstones to Kafka topic for downstream consumers
Backpressure: when the joiner cache is saturated, fall back to best-effort tagging (join_token only) and emit a throttled backpressure metric; do not drop original log payloads
Hot store path: map join_token and tenant labels to Loki stream labels and an ES index template that avoids high-cardinality freeform labels (attributes moved to a single 'attrs' json field for ES)

Cold path: aggregator compacts logs into Parquet with schema registry encoded column types; write to S3 with 7-day hot/hybrid window before flipping to cold; lifecycle policies will then move to Glacier/cheaper tiers
Dedupe and idempotency: ingest writes idempotency tokens (log_id + producer_id) to a small RocksDB layer during ingestion to prevent duplicate writes during retries
Observability: add dashboards for join_token success rate, joiner cache hit rate, per-tenant hot/cold bytes, and error budget impact; add alert when join_token join rate drops below threshold
Security: ensure join_token generation does not include PII; use tenant-scoped salts stored in KMS and rotated quarterly
Compatibility: provide a transitional header for older agents that only emit trace_id; joiner will synthesize a join_token from trace_id and best-effort timestamp rounding
progress_updates: 2025-02-15: Ticket created after incidents where trace->log joins were failing for peak tenants. Initial design sketched in Observability RFC.
2025-02-20: PoC for join_token computation completed (Arjun). Benchmarked sha256 + base62 truncation -- acceptable performance at 20k qps.
2025-02-25: Design review with infra and security. Decided on tenant-scoped KMS salt to avoid cross-tenant correlation; security review flagged key rotation requirements.

2025-02-28: Implemented edge parser normalization and small integration test against local Loki instance. Observed high-label cardinality when attributes were flattened; switched to single 'attrs' field for ES paths.

2025-03-03: Joiner service skeleton merged (PR #4821). Added basic cache eviction metrics and a failing e2e test for trace->log linking under load. Next: optimize cache size heuristic and implement Parquet writer component.
risks_and_mitigation: High cardinality labels may still slip into Loki: mitigate by enforcing label whitelist and moving rich attributes into the 'attrs' json blob
Cache mis-sizing could cause join misses under flash traffic: mitigation is autoscaling joiner replicas and making miss-rate a key SLO
Extra ingest latency from joiner sync calls: design to be asynchronous with best-effort tagging to avoid backpressure on producers
Cold-tier cost estimate uncertainty: run a cost model on 30-day sample of current logs before finalizing retention defaults
